attributes.content: A running shoe should leave a thumb’s width in front of your longest toe. Try shoes in the afternoon, when your feet are a little bigger, and wear the socks you run in.

More foam feels soft on long runs and protects your joints on hard roads. Less foam gives you a closer feel of the ground, which many runners like for short, fast sessions.

The drop is the height difference between heel and toe. A higher drop (8–12 mm) suits heel strikers; a lower drop (0–6 mm) encourages a mid-foot landing.

Road shoes have flat, durable rubber. Trail shoes have deep lugs that bite into mud and gravel – they feel clumsy on asphalt and wear down fast there.
